children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you check your eligibility for Child Benefit! Let me start by retrieving the assessment framework.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking you about your child or children.

**First, I need to know about the child/children you're claiming for:**

1. **How many children are you applying for Child Benefit?**
2. **What is the age of each child?** (Please provide their name and date of birth, or just their current age)

This will help me determine which eligibility pathway applies to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about one child - Alex, who is 14 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thanks for providing that information. So we're checking eligibility for **Alex, who is 14 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, this is good news - children under 16 generally qualify for Child Benefit as long as certain conditions are met. Let me now check those conditions.

**My next question for you:**

Is Alex currently working full-time (30 hours or more per week)?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: **Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is Alex not in paid work at all?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. They're just focused on school right now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's great - Alex is not in paid work and is focused on school. Let me continue checking the other eligibility requirements.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**My next question:**

Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right, such as:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit
- Other similar state benefits

In other words, is Alex not claiming any of these benefits for themselves?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - Alex isn't getting any benefits in their own name. They're only 14, so they don't claim anything themselves.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's helpful. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**My next question:**

Is Alex in any kind of apprenticeship? If so, what type and in which country (England, Scotland, Wales)?

If Alex is not in an apprenticeship at all, just let me know that - that would be the simplest scenario given they're only 14 and focused on school.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in an apprenticeship. Like I said, they're just in school - they're only 14.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is in school and not in an apprenticeship. Let me move on to the next important check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now I need to check your residency situation:**

This is an important part of the eligibility assessment. Can you tell me:

1. **Where do you normally live?** (Do you normally live in the UK?)

2. **If you're not normally resident in the UK, do you have any of the following:**
   - Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
   - Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
   - Are you a Crown servant living abroad or in certain qualifying countries?

Most people will answer that they normally live in the UK, which would be the straightforward path. But let me know your situation so I can check the right residency requirements.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't live in the UK - I live abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thanks for clarifying that. Since you live abroad, I need to understand your specific situation better so I can check which residency pathway might apply to you.

Can you tell me more about your circumstances:

1. **Are you a Crown servant?** (For example, working for the UK government, Foreign Office, or in certain qualifying roles abroad?)

2. **Do you have any immigration status under the EU Settlement Scheme?** (Either settled status or pre-settled status?)

3. **If you have pre-settled status, can you tell me:**
   - Are you working and earning above the National Insurance threshold (or expecting to)?
   - Are you actively looking for work?
   - Do you have sufficient resources to support yourself and your family financially?
   - Are you studying?
   - Are you a family member of an EEA or Swiss national?

These details will help me determine if there's a pathway for you to qualify for Child Benefit while living abroad.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant, and I don't have any settled or pre-settled status. I'm just living abroad - I don't work for the UK government or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Unfortunately, based on what you've told me, it appears that you don't meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit.

Let me confirm the key points:
- You normally live abroad (not in the UK)
- You don't have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- You're not a Crown servant living abroad

Since you don't fall into any of the approved residency pathways, let me navigate to the formal outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me provide you with the formal assessment outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Assessment Result: **INELIGIBLE**

**Why you're not eligible:**

You do not meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit. While Alex would otherwise qualify as a 14-year-old dependent child who is in school and not working, **the claimant (the person claiming the benefit) must normally live in the UK** to be eligible.

Currently, you live abroad and do not have any of the special circumstances that would allow you to claim from outside the UK:
- ✗ You don't have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- ✗ You don't have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- ✗ You're not a Crown servant living abroad

---

**What this means:**

Child Benefit is only payable to people who normally live in the UK, or who meet very specific exceptions. Living abroad without one of these approved statuses means you cannot claim Child Benefit for Alex, regardless of Alex's circumstances.

**If your situation changes:**

If you move back to the UK in the future, or if you obtain settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme and meet the qualifying criteria, you would then be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex (as long as Alex remains under 16 or meets the 16-19 education criteria).

**For more information:**

You can find more details at: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this decision?

reasonings: Alex is 14 years old, which would normally qualify them as a dependent child. Alex is not working full-time, is not receiving benefits in their own right, and is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship - all of which are positive factors. However, the claimant (Alex's parent/guardian) does not meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit. The claimant normally lives abroad and does not have settled status, pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or Crown servant status. Therefore, even though Alex would otherwise qualify as a child, the claimant is ineligible because they do not meet the residency requirements that apply to the person claiming on behalf of the child.
arguments.overall_reasoning: The claimant is ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex because they do not normally live in the UK and do not meet any of the special residency circumstances (such as settled/pre-settled EU Settlement Scheme status or Crown servant status). Child Benefit eligibility requires the claimant to normally reside in the UK or meet one of these special circumstances. While Alex meets all the child-related eligibility criteria, the claimant's residency status is a barrier to eligibility."
